articles.title: The Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group Announces New Hours for Winter
articles.deck: Residents of Cedar Hollow filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 19 weeks once it begins. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings.

articles.title: Esther Emerson, 87, Longtime Volunteer

body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge.

Born in Hickory Ridge in the years after the war, Esther Emerson spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Esther Emerson died in April at home on Coal Place, at the age of 87.

articles.title: Council Tables Saturday Cleanup Day Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 9 residents spoke at Saturday’s session.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Councilmember Yolanda Kessler asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500. Residents of Cedar Hollow said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Public works estimates the work will take about 9 weeks once it starts in June.

articles.title: Letter: The Community Oven on Wren Street Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the December meeting. To the editor: I have lived on Wren Street for 37 years, and I want to say what a difference St. Brendan’s Parish has made.
Please keep the community oven in the budget. Many of us on Wren Street use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the December meeting.
Cyrus Moffat, Foundry Row

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group
